title: cPoker Hydra Case Study: Implement Interactive dApp

ms.promise:
Source code and documentation on https://github.com/Cardano-After-Dark/hydra-poc

ms.criteria:
Verify the feasibility of implementing a testnet smart contract that will:
・Lock funds for a number of participants, in order to start a game
・Enable performing in-game transactions directly on Hydra
・Release funds at game conclusion according to the results of the game
ms.report:
The milestone outputs are available in the GitHub Repo https://github.com/Cardano-After-Dark/hydra-poc/tree/blog:
・Article with feasibility study : docs/blog/ms1.md
・Implementation of the smart contract --> dred smart contract

In the article we demonstrate it is possible to implement a testnet smart contract with 
・funds locking --> Yes, feasible
・perform in-app transactions on Hydra --> See ms1.md, section "Real-World Technical Insights"
・release funds when the application protocol terminates --> See ms1.md section "Looking Forward"

As evidence for the milestone completion, we produced the following resources:
・Article with feasibility study: See ms1.md
・Implementation of the smart contract handling transactions on Hydra --> dred smart contract
・Source code for the Hydra PoC implementation --> See scripts 
・Video Report --> See YouTube Video Hydra PoC M1.

As additional content, we include also
・README explaining the project 
・Tutorial1: Cardano Hydra PoC First Run
・Tutorial2: Cardano Hydra PoC Local (same tutorial used in the YouTube Video)

Related to your requests in the previous review, please, see the newly added sections, and the new changes in the article: 
・References: added a YouTube Playlist "Hydra PoC - Building Interactive dApps on Cardano"
・Transaction Hash Visibility: As the interaction happens on L2 (Hydra), the transaction hashes are not visible on the L1 (Cardano preprod) network, so they are lost when closing the Hydra Head.

ms.criteria:
Verify the feasibility of implementing a group cryptographic protocol using Hydra similar to what is presented in the Kaleidoscope paper, with focus on:
・Implementing an exchange between participants to agree on a shared key
・Enable participants to perform encryptions (and notify others)
・Enable participants to perform decryptions (and notify others)
